name: Electro-Harmonix Electric Mistress (1976 V2, Filter Matrix)
description: 1976 Electric Mistress V2 (PCB EH-5200-1-A), the first version with the FLANGE / FILTER MATRIX switch. 18 V (2 x 9 V) regulated to about 13.3 V by a CA741 + BC309 series regulator off a 6.8 V zener; the same divider sets the audio/BBD bias through the BIAS trimmer. Audio: 0.1 uF / 5k6 into a CA1458 follower, then an inverting summing stage with treble pre-emphasis (470 + 4k7||47n in, 6k8 feedback) that also takes the COLOR regeneration on its + input through 4.7 nF. Its output drives both inputs of a Reticon SAD1024 whose two 512-stage sections run in parallel on the same clocks (OUT A' and OUT B tied, 10k + 3.3 nF load), and the dry path (47 nF + 13k). The BBD output goes through 47 nF to the FEEDBACK trimmer (100k || 7k5) and COLOR pot (with 470 + 47 nF de-emphasis) and through 10k to the passive mix node, which has the matching 470 + 47 nF de-emphasis. LFO: an LM339 used as a Miller integrator (2.2 uF) charged through the 1M reverse-log RATE pot from a CD4013 SR latch (Q 33k / Qbar 10k), with an LM339 set comparator at 0.44 V and a 680k/1M reset divider, giving a 0.45-10.6 V triangle; RANGE (100K lin) scales it (or a 39k static source in FILTER MATRIX) into the VCO control. The VCO (BC177 current source, 470 pF, LM339 pair, 1N914, CD4013 divide-by-2; 18-280 kHz) is the bbd clock table.

sources.title: Ralf Metzger, 'Electric Mistress Mystery Page': 1976 Electric Mistress V2 (EH-5200-1-A) page, parts list (CA1458, SAD1024, SCL4013BE, CA339G, CA741CE; BC309C, BC177A; 1x bias, 1x feedback trimmer; 2x 9 V or 18 V) and redrawn schematic 1976-electric-mistress-v2-schematic.gif (all values in this netlist; dashed parts factory-added on the copper side)
Ralf Metzger, 1976 Electric Mistress V1 page: V1 = V2 circuit with an On/Off switch in place of FLANGE/FILTER MATRIX
Ralf Metzger, history page: first sold 1976, filter matrix switch added soon after; 1977-82 small changes, many PCBs
Ralf Metzger, 'How it works': LFO (SR-latch 4013, 0.4 V set, 0.6*VLFO reset at about 6 V, Q/Qbar 3 V / 9 V drive), VCO (BC177 current source, 470 pF, LM339 pair, 4013 divide-by-2)

Ralf Metzger, measurements: V2 frequency response, comb filter at min/max feedback, LFO at slowest sweep (0.067 Hz, 0.45-10.6 V at the RANGE wiper), V2 VCO delay vs VLFO (1.15 ms at 0.5 V to 10.75 ms at 9.6 V)
Ralf Metzger, voltages (V4 board, same topology): V+ 13.00 V, divider 11.83 / 6.61 / 0.44 / 0.09 V, IC4a pin 4 6.59-6.61 V, Q/Qbar 0.03-12.91 V, RESET 0.31-6.18 V
Ralf Metzger, alignment: bias for max clean swing at SAD1024 pin 6/12 with 200 Hz (> 1 Vpp); feedback trim just before oscillation (COLOR, RANGE max, RATE mid)
Ralf Metzger, BBD page: SAD1024 2 x 512 stages run in parallel in the Mistress; delay = stages / (2 fclock)

EG&G Reticon SAD-1024 / SAD-512 data sheet (1977): pinout, VDD 10-17 V (15 typ), VBB = VDD-1, fs 1.5 kHz-1.5 MHz, clock line 110 pF, Cin 7 pF, optimum input bias +6 V at 15 V clocks, max input 1-2 Vpp, gain 1.2 typ (load dependent, Fig. 6), output followers about 400 Ohm, THD vs level (Fig. 5), S/N > 70 dB, delay = 512 clock half periods
R.G. Keen (GEOFEX), SAD-1024 data sheet transcription
Texas Instruments LM339 data sheet (SLCS006): large-signal gain 200 V/mV, response time 1.3 us (5 mV overdrive) / 0.3 us (TTL-level step), output sink 16 mA typ, open collector
DIYstompboxes forum, 'Question on how the SAD1024 is used in the Electric Mistress' (both sections paralleled, not the datasheet's clock-swapped multiplex)

OC_SAT.note: unverified: stand-in for the LM339 open-collector saturation (Vf 0.13 V at 0.13 mA, 0.21 V at 2.8 mA; leakage 1 uA)

LM339_DRV.note: unverified: drive stage of the behavioural LM339: A0 200 V/mV (TI LM339 datasheet, large-signal voltage gain typ); GBW/slew assumed

CD4013_LATCH.note: unverified: behavioural CMOS latch core (rail-to-rail; CD4013B outputs swing within 50 mV of the rails at light load)

parts.note: unverified: behavioural LM339 section: a macro comparator (its output falls to 0 V when V(+) < V(-)) pulls the output down through a low-drop diode = the open-collector output (about 0.1-0.2 V saturation at the 0.1-3 mA used here; the 16 mA sink limit is not modelled). A real NPN output stage would make each section 4 nonlinear ports and the LFO loop group 10. Dynamic response not fitted: here the LM339s act only at LFO rates; the fast pair IC4c/IC4d is inside the clock table
CMOS input: no current

unverified: set so that RESET trips at 6.2 V (Metzger V4 reading: the RESET pin peaks at 6.18 V with V+ 13.00 V); the latch resets when R > V(l) - 0.515 VDD and sets when S > 0.515 VDD. CD4013B datasheet: typ. VDD/2, from Metzger's V4 reading (RESET pin peaks at 6.18 V with V+ 13.00 V, where the latch flips); CD4013B datasheet: typ. VDD/2
Q goes high when L + S - R > VDD/2: set at S > VDD/2, reset at R > VDD/2, hold otherwise
unverified: CMOS output resistance at 13 V (CD4013B datasheet class, about 0.4-1 kOhm)
Qbar = VDD - Q

controls.label: Rate
controls.note: RATE 1M reverse-log rheostat in the LFO integrator. 0.067 Hz (measured slowest, Metzger) to about 10 Hz

controls.label: Range
controls.note: RANGE 100K lin: in flange mode it scales the LFO swing reaching the VCO (sweep depth and its top end); in Filter Matrix mode it is the manual delay (comb) setting. Legacy 'Depth'

controls.label: Filter Matrix
controls.note: FLANGE (0) / FILTER MATRIX (1) toggle: matrix disconnects the LFO from RANGE and feeds it from V+ through 39k (static comb). Legacy 'Static'

controls.label: Bias trim (internal)
controls.note: VR1: audio/BBD bias = 6.8 V * position. Factory: maximum clean swing at SAD1024 pin 6/12 with a 200 Hz sine (Metzger alignment). Default 0.78 = 5.3 V, the datasheet's +6 V optimum (15 V clocks) scaled to the 13.3 V clock. unverified: no published V2 bias reading

controls.label: Feedback trim (internal)
controls.note: VR2 100k rheostat (in parallel with 7k5) setting the maximum regeneration. Factory: just below self-oscillation at COLOR max. unverified default

controls.label: Sync
controls.note: No tempo sync in the pedal; stored only

controls.label: LED
controls.note: The 1976 V2 has no status LED; stored only

controls.label: Invert
controls.note: No polarity switch; the wet/dry polarity is fixed by the circuit. Stored only

controls.label: Rotate
controls.note: No LFO phase control; stored only

controls.label: Mix
controls.note: Dry/wet fixed by the 13k (dry) / 10k (wet) passive mix; no control. Stored only

parts.label: V+ (regulated, 12.0-13.5 V)
parts.note: unverified: ideal source standing in for the real regulator: 18 V (2 x 9 V) -> BC309C series pass, CA741CE error amp (+ = 22k/30k divider, - = 6.8 V zener fed by 100k with 10 uF). The netlist value is the regulator's set point 6.8*(1 + 22k/(30k||100k VR1)) = 13.28 V (Metzger: 12.0-13.5 V; his V4 measured 13.00 V). Not modelled at circuit level: op-amp supply pins must be cut nodes and op-amp outputs cannot be, so the regulator loop (gain 2e5) has to cross the one-sample cut and the DC cut iteration does not converge. Battery sag is irrelevant behind the regulator

parts.label: Regulator feedback node (= zener voltage)
parts.note: unverified: the CA741 holds its + input (the 22k/30k divider node, which also feeds VR1) at the 6.8 V zener; ideal source (no zener model). The real zener's +/-5 % tolerance moves V+ and the bias range together

parts.label: VR1 BIAS trimmer
parts.note: VR1 100 kOhm from the regulator's 6.8 V feedback node to ground; its wiper is the audio/BBD bias line. Its 100 kOhm also loads the 30 kOhm divider leg, which is why V+ is 13.3 V rather than 11.8 V. Pin orientation (clockwise = higher bias) assumed

parts.label: IC1a input buffer
parts.note: unverified: Metzger's drawing labels IC1 '4558' but his V2 parts list and IC photo show a CA1458E (dual 741-class); library LM741 macro used

parts.label: Pre-emphasis cap (across 4k7): treble boost 720 Hz -> 7.2 kHz
IC1b summing amp (dry inverting x1.45 LF / x14.5 HF; feedback non-inverting) -> SAD1024 input
parts.note: unverified: CA1458E per the V2 parts list (see IC1A)

parts.label: IC2 Reticon SAD1024: both 512-stage sections in parallel, same clocks
parts.note: Pins (Reticon datasheet): IN A 2 and IN B 15 tied to IC1b out; phi1A 8 + phi1B 10 tied, phi2A 3 + phi2B 14 tied (4013 Q / Qbar, IC3b pins 13/12); OUT A' 6 and OUT B 12 tied (used), OUT A 5 and OUT B' 11 tied to VDD (unused outputs, as the datasheet requires); VDD 7 and VBB 9 at V+ (13.0-13.3 V, 100 uF decoupling factory-added); GND 1; NC 4/13/16 grounded. Delay = 512 half clock periods = 256/fclk (datasheet). The two used outputs are the opposite-phase half-period outputs of two identical lines, i.e. the engine's out1/out2 pair. The clock table is fclk (the 4013 output, half the comparator VCO rate) versus the RANGE wiper voltage, from an ngspice run of the real VCO (BC177 + 470 pF + LM339 IC4c/IC4d + 1N914 + CD4013) at V+ = 13.28 V; see the notes. Below 0.1 V the VCO stalls (IC4c + below the reset threshold); the circuit never goes there (wiper minimum about 0.1 V). unverified: SAD1024 model parameters must be added to the library (datasheet facts in the notes); the comparator delay in the VCO deck is the LM339 datasheet response time (0.3 us), not a measurement

parts.label: BBD output termination (source-follower load)
parts.note: 10 kOhm termination: datasheet Fig. 6 gives gain about 1.0 at 10 kOhm (0.75 at 1 kOhm, 1.25 at 50 kOhm)

parts.label: VR2 FEEDBACK trimmer (rheostat)
parts.note: unverified: factory trim is by ear: 'just before oscillation with COLOR and RANGE at maximum, RATE at mid' (Metzger alignment page). Default 0.1 = 90 kOhm (in parallel with 7k5: 6.9 kOhm, the least-feedback end). The engine owner should re-trim with the real bbd block. Wiper tied to the top end as drawn

parts.label: COLOR (10K lin)
parts.note: Regeneration amount: wiper -> 4.7 nF -> IC1b +. Clockwise = more feedback (Metzger alignment: COLOR max = CW)

parts.label: Output de-emphasis C (600 Hz -> 7.2 kHz shelf, mirrors the pre-emphasis)

parts.note: 150 Ohm on the V2 drawing (130 Ohm on the V4)

parts.label: IC4a LM339 (CA339G) used as a Miller integrator: + = 6.6 V divider, - = nn, open collector -> VLFO
parts.note: Measured V4: pin 4 6.59-6.61 V = pin 5 6.61 V, i.e. it runs linear (virtual ground)

parts.label: 0.22 uF on the integrator input, factory-added (dashed)
RATE (1M rev log)
parts.note: Rheostat on the wiper-to-pin-3 segment: R = 1M*(1 - t(x)). CCW = maximum resistance = slowest (Metzger). Measured slowest sweep 0.067 Hz (V2); this netlist: T = 13.3 us/Ohm * (R + 7.7k)

parts.label: From 4013 Q
parts.note: Q -> 33k, Qbar -> 10k: the charge/discharge drive is 3.0 V or 9.9 V against the 6.6 V virtual ground (Metzger)

parts.label: IC4b LM339: SET when VLFO < 0.44 V
RESET divider bottom (RESET = 0.6*VLFO, trips at about V+/2)
IC3a CD4013 used as an SR latch (C and D grounded)
parts.note: unverified: the engine has no CMOS logic; this is a behavioural stand-in (macro comparator with positive feedback, threshold V+/2, Q/Qbar through 470 Ohm). Report: CMOS gate/flip-flop primitive needed

parts.label: LFO start kick
parts.note: Simulation aid, not in the pedal: 1 mV through 10 MOhm into the integrator node starts the relaxation loop from its DC balance point

parts.label: Filter Matrix source (39k, factory-added on the V2)
FLANGE / FILTER MATRIX: matrix throw (static, 39k from V+)
RANGE (100K lin)
parts.note: Top = LFO (flange) or 39k from V+ (matrix); bottom = 4k7 to the 0.09 V divider node. Wiper = IC4c pin 7 = the VCO control (Metzger's VLFO measurement point). Clockwise = toward the top = longer delay (Metzger: RANGE max = CW)
